{"result":"{\"id\": \"page_liveops_calendar\", \"space_id\": \"space_OPS\", \"parent_id\": \"page_ops_home\", \"title\": \"Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning\", \"body\": \"

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). This page is the single source of truth for what live-ops events are scheduled, on which game, and at what cadence. It pairs with the runtime that actually fires these events — for architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage, see Live-Ops Event Engine. Event goals are set against the metrics bar tracked in Product OKRs — 2025 H1.

Event calendar

Every timed event we have run or currently run across the portfolio. \\\"Cadence\\\" is how the slot recurs; \\\"status\\\" is where the event stands as of the latest planning review.

EventGameCadenceStatus
Nathan's Treasure HuntDomino Delights (\\\"Game of Dominoes\\\" / GoD)One-off seasonalShipped Apr 2025
Win & CollectDomino DelightsOne-off seasonalShipped Sep 2024
River RushDomino DelightsOne-off seasonalShipped Jan 2025
Plague RaceZombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\")RecurringLive; algo bug Aug 2025
Zombie LaneZombie Match 3DOne-off seasonalShipped Jul 2025
Endless Monster ModeZombie Match 3DRecurring monthly (from Jun 2025)Live

Notes on individual events

  • Nathan's Treasure Hunt — our best-performing GoD seasonal to date; the reward-ladder structure is the template we now reuse for one-off events.
  • Plague Race — the recurring ranked competition on ZM3D. A scoring/matchmaking algorithm bug surfaced in Aug 2025 and skewed leaderboard settlement; treat pre-fix cohorts with caution when reading event revenue.
  • Endless Monster Mode — a monthly recurring mode that has become the reliable mid-month engagement beat since Jun 2025. This is the anchor slot the calendar is built around.

July 2025 scheduler outage. The event/lives scheduler stalled for roughly two weeks in July 2025, so scheduled events did not fire and the published calendar diverged from what players actually saw. Do not backfill or reason about that window from this calendar — the Live-Ops Event Engine page holds the reconstructed timeline and the revenue impact.

Planning cadence

We are a ~16-person studio, so live-ops planning is deliberately lightweight — one recurring meeting and one shared calendar, not a dedicated ops team. The working rhythm:

  • Weekly slotting review (Mondays). Design (Julia) and Growth (Frederick) walk the next four weeks: which recurring slots fire (Endless Monster Mode monthly, Plague Race on its ranked cadence) and whether a one-off seasonal drops on top.
  • Two-week content lock. Event config — reward tables, windows, cohort targeting — must be authored and reviewed at least two weeks before the window opens, so QA has a full sprint to validate on staging.
  • No overlapping recurring competitions. We do not run two ranked events on the same game at once; it splits the leaderboard population and muddies the revenue read.
  • Post-event read. Each event gets a short retro against its target from Product OKRs before the slot is reused.

The recurring slots (Endless Monster Mode monthly; Plague Race ranked) are the backbone of the calendar. One-off seasonals like Nathan's Treasure Hunt are layered on for spikes — they are the exception, not the base cadence, and should never displace a recurring slot without sign-off from Frederick.

{"result":"{\"id\": \"page_backend_services\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_arch_overview\", \"title\": \"Backend Services \\u2014 Elixir/Phoenix\", \"body\": \"

This page describes the Elixir/Phoenix backend services that sit behind the Harmony Games clients \\u2014 Domino Delights (\\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"/GoD internally), Zombie Match 3D (\\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" in-store), and Combo Fighter. The services own authoritative game state, player profiles, quests, and live-ops delivery. For the wider system picture and how these tie into Unity and Nakama, see Architecture Overview; realtime multiplayer and matchmaking are documented separately in Nakama Server Setup & Operations.

Ownership is deliberately thin \\u2014 a ~16-person studio can't staff a service mesh. One Elixir umbrella app, one Aurora cluster, a handful of Fargate tasks. Prefer boring and observable over clever.

Runtime & deployment

All services run as a single Elixir umbrella project, released with mix release and packaged into one container image. We run separate ECS Fargate services off that image (state, profile, quests, live-ops) so we can scale and roll them independently without maintaining separate codebases. Persistence is a shared Aurora PostgreSQL cluster with a schema per bounded context; the reader endpoint is used for analytics-adjacent queries so we don't contend with write traffic.

  • Compute: ECS Fargate, one task definition per service, behind an internal ALB.
  • Data: Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-AZ), Ecto for access, migrations gated in CI.
  • Infra as code: everything provisioned via AWS CDK \\u2014 VPC, clusters, task definitions, and Aurora are all defined in the CDK app so environments (staging/prod) stay in lockstep.

Auth

There is no third-party auth broker. A small custom identity service issues short-lived JWTs on login; every other service validates the JWT signature locally (no per-request network hop) and trusts the sub claim as the player ID. Device-bound refresh tokens are stored in the identity service's own schema. Live-ops and quest mutations additionally require an internal service token \\u2014 never a player JWT.

Services

ServiceResponsibilityDatastore
identityLogin, JWT issuance/rotation, device bindingAurora (schema: identity)
game_stateAuthoritative match/board state, progression, save reconciliationAurora (schema: state)
profilePlayer profile, inventory, wallet (coins/lives)Aurora (schema: profile)
questsQuest definitions, assignment, and completion trackingAurora (schema: quests)
live_opsEvent scheduling, feature-flag delivery, seasonal contentAurora (schema: liveops)

Endpoints & releasing

Phoenix serves a thin JSON API \\u2014 no HTML, no channels here (realtime lives in Nakama). Routes are versioned under /api/v1 and health-checked at /healthz for the ALB. A representative controller and the release command:

{"result":"{\"id\": \"page_nakama_setup\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_arch_overview\", \"title\": \"Nakama Server Setup & Operations\", \"body\": \"

This page covers how we run Nakama (the open-source game server) for Harmony Games' live titles — deploy, admin console access, and database migration ops. Nakama backs social and live-ops features (friends, leaderboards, storage) for Domino Delights (Game of Dominoes, internal codename GoD) and Zombie Match 3D. For the wider picture see Architecture Overview, and for VPC / cluster details see AWS Infrastructure Guide.

Runtime topology

Nakama ships as a single Docker image and runs on ECS Fargate behind an HTTPS Application Load Balancer. It uses the shared Aurora PostgreSQL cluster for state — we do not run a dedicated database for the game server. The ALB terminates TLS and forwards to the container over two listeners:

  • gRPC socket / client API on port 7350
  • HTTP admin + metrics on port 7351
  • Health check hits the Nakama healthcheck endpoint; the target group marks a task healthy on a 200

Task sizing

EnvironmentMemoryvCPU unitsClient portAdmin portBacking store
Prod~3072 MiB102473507351Aurora PostgreSQL (shared)
Dev~2048 MiB102473507351Aurora PostgreSQL (shared)

Prod runs a little hotter on memory because live-ops (leaderboard resets, Plague Race payouts) spikes storage writes. If a task keeps getting OOM-killed, bump memory before touching CPU — Nakama is memory-bound long before it is CPU-bound at our concurrency.

Deploy

Deploys are a rolling ECS service update: push the tagged image to ECR, then update the service to the new task definition revision. The ALB drains connections on the old task before it stops. Roll back by pointing the service at the previous task definition revision — do not delete old revisions.

bash

Admin console & DB migrations

Admin console

The Nakama admin console is served on port 7351 and is reachable only from inside the VPC — hit it via the internal hostname (e.g. social-admin.internal) over the VPN, never a public domain. Credentials live in Secrets Manager; the console is read-mostly in prod — use it to inspect accounts, storage objects, and leaderboard state, not to hand-edit live data.

Database migrations

Nakama owns its own schema inside the Aurora cluster and applies migrations on boot. Migration notes for operators:

  • Migrations run automatically when a new image starts; a failed migration fails the health check, so the bad task never takes traffic.
  • Before a version bump that includes a schema change, snapshot the Aurora cluster.
  • Never run two different Nakama image versions against the same database at once — keep the rolling deploy to a single version transition.

Nakama migrations are forward-only. There is no automatic down-migration — recovery from a bad schema change is restore-from-snapshot, so take the snapshot first. All server logs go to CloudWatch with a 1-month retention window; pull the failing task's log stream there when a deploy stalls in PROVISIONING.

— Douglas, Platform/Backend

What seems to be going wrong \\u2014 in plain English\\n   Symptom Likely Root Cause Who\\u2019s Feeling It     *Android tutorial-completion (and other funnel) rates look abnormally low* Analytics is splitting one real person into two \\u201cusers\\u201d: \\u2022 *Firebase-generated ID (A)* created automatically at *`first_app_open`*. \\u2022 *Backend/Game ID (B)* that we explicitly set later via `setUserId()` once the player finishes login. Any session in which the hand-off from A \\u2192 B never happens, or happens but historical events aren\\u2019t re-keyed.   *Dashboards show large blocks of \\u201corphan\\u201d events whose `user_id` doesn\\u2019t match the Singular ID or in-game ID* Join logic in Metabase / BigQuery expects a _single_ stable key. When events carry mixed keys, rows fail to join, so funnels drop users after _Begin Level 1_. Mostly _new Android installs_ (fresh Firebase IDs) and possibly _returning users_ who reinstall or clear data before we re-attach their backend ID.   *Counts differ across sources (Firebase vs Singular vs Backend)* Each system sees a different identifier set and reconciliation rules are inconsistent. Anyone whose ID mapping never resolves or resolves after the reporting window.\\n2. Current ID life-cycle (what we _think_ happens)\\n1. *Install / first launch*\\n2.  _Firebase SDK_ fires *`first_app_open`* with a _Firebase-generated_ anonymous ID (call it *F-ID*).\\n3. *Player reaches login / registration screen*\\n4.  Game calls backend \\u2192 backend returns a *Backend Player UUID* (call it *B-ID*).\\n5. *App code executes `analytics.setUserId(B-ID)`* for _Firebase_ and *`setCustomUserId(B-ID)`* (or equivalent) for _Singular_.\\n6. *Expectation*:\\n7.  _From this point forward_ every event carries *B-ID*, and analytics pipelines stitch early events from F-ID onto B-ID.\\n8. *Reality* (android):\\n9.  _Sometimes_ step 3 never fires, fires after a crash, or doesn\\u2019t propagate to all SDKs \\u2192 events remain tagged with F-ID. Downstream, your dbt model (`zm_flattened_pre`) can\\u2019t join those rows to gameplay events (which _do_ have B-ID), so the player appears to churn instantly.\\n3. Key unknowns blocking a fix\\n   Area Unknown Why It Matters     *Instrumentation* Under what exact conditions does `setUserId()` execute? Is it guarded by a login success callback, a coroutine that can be cancelled, or an async error? If the call never runs, we must move it earlier or add retries.   *ID Reconciliation* Does Firebase automatically retro-link earlier F-ID events to B-ID once `setUserId()` fires? Is There a _time limit_ or _offline_ edge-case where this fails? Determines whether we can rely on Firebase stitching or must backfill ourselves in ETL.   *SDK parity* Are we sending B-ID to *all* analytics/attribution SDKs (Firebase, Singular, Unity Ads, internal event bus) in the same frame? Mismatches create double counting and attribution gaps.   *Platform difference* iOS appears healthy. What differences exist in Android init order, Gradle config, or privacy-sandbox settings? Narrowing to Android-specific code paths will speed triage.   *user segments* Is the problem limited to: \\u2022 _Brand-new installs_ on Android \\u2265 v0.3.8? \\u2022 _Return users_ who reinstall? \\u2022 Players coming from a specific UA source (e.g., Unity Ads)? Lets us reproduce and create a focused test cohort.   *Data pipeline* In `zm_flattened_pre`, which field is the _primary key_ we expect (`user_pseudo_id` or backend `user_id`)? Do we ever overwrite it? Wrong join key = lost rows even if IDs are set correctly on the device.\\n4. Targeted questions for tomorrow\\u2019s debugging session\\n*A. Do we clear or regenerate B-ID on logout, update, or data-wipe?\\n4. Can we add a debug log to print both F-ID and B-ID on first 5 events of a session?\\n*B. Backend / Auth (Simon)*\\n 4. At what point in the auth flow do we issue B-ID? Could a timeout / partial failure leave the client without an ID?\\n 5. Do we ever re-issue a _new_ B-ID for an existing account (e.g., migration, merge)? If so, how do we tell analytics about the change?\\n*C. Analytics SDK & Attribution (Blake)*\\n 6. input.title: Live-Ops scheduler resilience — build the July 2025 outage remediation (recurred Nov 2025)
input.description:
## Why this ticket exists

The Zombie Match 3D live-ops event/lives scheduler has now failed the **same way twice**, and the remediation written up after the first failure was never built. This ticket exists so that work stops falling through the cracks. **Owners: Douglas (scheduler/backend) + Arthur Blake.**

### It happened twice (same failure mode)
- **Jul 12–26, 2025 (summer outage).** The event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. First player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating (~03:41 UTC Jul 13). No scheduled events fired for ~2 weeks; store revenue dipped ~30% across the window. Warehouse `LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE` records Plague Race (Jul 7) and Zombie Lane (Jul 14) as **failed — "backend scheduler stopped; events not firing for 2 weeks."** No standalone ticket was cut at the time.
- **~Nov 10 – early Dec 2025 (recurrence).** Endless Monster Mode (Nov 10) is recorded as **degraded — "tournament scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks"**: 526 participants vs ~2,000 for a healthy EMM, 7% completion vs ~47%, $11 event revenue vs ~$316. Support flagged tournaments not restarting for weeks and players losing lives/refills with no way to earn them back. It was resolved only after a manual restart (Plague Race Dec 8 completed normally).

### Real impact of the recurrence (warehouse = source of truth)
- Nov 10 Endless Monster Mode event: ~75% fewer participants, ~97% less event revenue vs a healthy EMM.
- Zombie Match 3D daily revenue: avg ~$151/day (Oct 20–Nov 9) → ~$131/day (Nov 10–Dec 7), a **~13% dip (~$545 lost vs baseline)**; DAU fell ~12% (4,435 → 3,904) over the same window. (Some of this overlaps ZM3D's broader decline, but the loss of the reason-to-return loop is a clear contributor and mirrors July.)
- Player-facing: lives/refills not regenerating with no way to earn them back — see linked open tickets ZOM-667 and ENG-2400.

## Broken by design, not a fresh regression
Confirmed against `harmonygames-Games/match3d-backend`:
- `lib/zombies_game/scheduler.ex` is a **Quantum** in-process cron (`use Quantum`), started in `application.ex` as a single **Highlander** global singleton (`{Highlander, ZombiesGame.Scheduler}`) — one active process, no hot standby / fast-failover monitoring.
- Event resets ("tournament restarts") are **self-registered Quantum jobs**: each leaderboard GenServer (`leaderboards/server.ex`) reads its cron `schedule` at boot and calls `Scheduler.new_job |> add_job |> activate_job`. If that one scheduler stalls or a job isn't (re)registered, every event reset silently stops.
- Life regeneration is **coupled to the same scheduler loop** (documented in the Live-Ops Event Engine page), so one stall takes down events **and** lives at once.
- There is **no external watchdog / heartbeat / missed-tick alert**: `Observability & Alerting` (updated Aug 2025, i.e. *after* the summer outage) alarms on API 5xx, Aurora, Kinesis lag and crash spikes — nothing on the scheduler's last tick. Both outages ran for weeks before a human noticed.
- The latest backend commit (Oct 12, 2025, "Fix zombie lane one off") and surrounding history is feature work — no resilience code shipped. **Conclusion: this is the known architectural single-point-of-failure recurring, not a new code regression.**

## Remediation that was promised (July 2025) and never built
From the Live-Ops Event Engine postmortem — none of these are in the codebase or ticketed:
1. **Heartbeat + external watchdog** that pages on a missed scheduler tick — target alert < 5 min, not 12+ hours / weeks.
2. **Decouple life regeneration from event firing** so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
3. **Leader election / real failover** so a second process can take over the tick loop (today Highlander gives a singleton but no missed-tick takeover).
4. **Lives-regeneration reconciler** that can catch a cohort back up after a stall.
5. **Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue** so drift is visible on one screen.
6. (New) Wire the watchdog into the on-call rota in Observability & Alerting.

## Acceptance
Watchdog alerts on a missed tick within 5 min in staging + prod; lives regen survives an event-scheduler stall; documented failover for the tick loop; last-tick + revenue on one dashboard; reconciler runbook. Update the Live-Ops Event Engine page when done.

Ref: Confluence "Live-Ops Event Engine" postmortem. Do not change live event config/scheduling as part of triage — this is the durable fix.

The Zombie Match 3D live-ops event/lives scheduler has now failed the **same way twice**, and the remediation written up after the first failure was never built. This ticket exists so that work stops falling through the cracks. **Owners: Douglas (scheduler/backend) + Arthur Blake.**

### It happened twice (same failure mode)
- **Jul 12–26, 2025 (summer outage).** The event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. First player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating (~03:41 UTC Jul 13). No scheduled events fired for ~2 weeks; store revenue dipped ~30% across the window. Warehouse `LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE` records Plague Race (Jul 7) and Zombie Lane (Jul 14) as **failed — "backend scheduler stopped; events not firing for 2 weeks."** No standalone ticket was cut at the time.
- **~Nov 10 – early Dec 2025 (recurrence).** Endless Monster Mode (Nov 10) is recorded as **degraded — "tournament scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks"**: 526 participants vs ~2,000 for a healthy EMM, 7% completion vs ~47%, $11 event revenue vs ~$316. Support flagged tournaments not restarting for weeks and players losing lives/refills with no way to earn them back. It was resolved only after a manual restart (Plague Race Dec 8 completed normally).

### Real impact of the recurrence (warehouse = source of truth)
- Nov 10 Endless Monster Mode event: ~75% fewer participants, ~97% less event revenue vs a healthy EMM.
- Zombie Match 3D daily revenue: avg ~$151/day (Oct 20–Nov 9) → ~$131/day (Nov 10–Dec 7), a **~13% dip (~$545 lost vs baseline)**; DAU fell ~12% (4,435 → 3,904) over the same window. (Some of this overlaps ZM3D's broader decline, but the loss of the reason-to-return loop is a clear contributor and mirrors July.)
- Player-facing: lives/refills not regenerating with no way to earn them back — see linked open tickets ZOM-667 and ENG-2400.

## Broken by design, not a fresh regression
Confirmed against `harmonygames-Games/match3d-backend`:
- `lib/zombies_game/scheduler.ex` is a **Quantum** in-process cron (`use Quantum`), started in `application.ex` as a single **Highlander** global singleton (`{Highlander, ZombiesGame.Scheduler}`) — one active process, no hot standby / fast-failover monitoring.

If that one scheduler stalls or a job isn't (re)registered, every event reset silently stops.
- Life regeneration is **coupled to the same scheduler loop** (documented in the Live-Ops Event Engine page), so one stall takes down events **and** lives at once.
- There is **no external watchdog / heartbeat / missed-tick alert**: `Observability & Alerting` (updated Aug 2025, i.e. *after* the summer outage) alarms on API 5xx, Aurora, Kinesis lag and crash spikes — nothing on the scheduler's last tick. Both outages ran for weeks before a human noticed.
- The latest backend commit (Oct 12, 2025, "Fix zombie lane one off") and surrounding history is feature work — no resilience code shipped. **Conclusion: this is the known architectural single-point-of-failure recurring, not a new code regression.**

## Remediation that was promised (July 2025) and never built
From the Live-Ops Event Engine postmortem — none of these are in the codebase or ticketed:
1. **Heartbeat + external watchdog** that pages on a missed scheduler tick — target alert < 5 min, not 12+ hours / weeks.
2. **Decouple life regeneration from event firing** so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
3. **Leader election / real failover** so a second process can take over the tick loop (today Highlander gives a singleton but no missed-tick takeover).
4. **Lives-regeneration reconciler** that can catch a cohort back up after a stall.
5. **Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue** so drift is visible on one screen.
6. (New) Wire the watchdog into the on-call rota in Observability & Alerting.

## Acceptance
Watchdog alerts on a missed tick within 5 min in staging + prod; lives regen survives an event-scheduler stall; documented failover for the tick loop; last-tick + revenue on one dashboard; reconciler runbook. Update the Live-Ops Event Engine page when done.

input.body:
The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D ("Puzzles vs Zombies" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content — Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode — and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the two outages it has caused: the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue, and its November 2025 recurrence. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

This has now failed the same way twice (Jul 2025 and Nov 2025), and none of the remediation below was built. Durable fix is now tracked in Linear ZOM-2438; owners Douglas + Arthur.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incidents below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

Implementation note (confirmed in harmonygames-Games/match3d-backend): the scheduler is a single in-process Quantum cron (lib/zombies_game/scheduler.ex) started as one Highlander global singleton in application.ex. Event resets ("tournament restarts") are self-registered Quantum jobs — each leaderboard GenServer reads its cron schedule at boot and adds a job. If that one scheduler stalls or a job is never re-registered, every event reset silently stops, and because lives ride the same loop, lives stop too.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12–26, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially — on the order of 30% across the outage — as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation (promised July 2025 — status: NOT built as of Jul 2026, now tracked in ZOM-2438)

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours). — not built
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both. — not built
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop. — not built (Highlander gives a singleton, but no missed-tick takeover)
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall. — not built
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen. — not built

November 2025 recurrence

Between roughly Nov 10 and early December 2025, the same event/lives scheduler stopped advancing again — tournaments/events stopped firing and were not restarted for weeks, and players again lost lives/refills with no way to earn them back. As in July, no standalone ticket was cut while it was happening; it was handled ad hoc in #live-incidents (support flagged tournaments not restarting for weeks) and only resolved after a manual restart — the Plague Race that opened Dec 8 settled normally.

Impact (warehouse = source of truth)

  • Endless Monster Mode (Nov 10, 2025) is recorded in LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE as degraded — "tournament scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks": 526 participants vs ~2,000 for a healthy EMM, 7% completion vs ~47%, and $11 event revenue vs ~$316.
  • Zombie Match 3D daily revenue fell from ~$151/day (Oct 20–Nov 9) to ~$131/day (Nov 10–Dec 7) — a ~13% dip, roughly $545 below baseline across the window — and DAU fell ~12% (4,435 → 3,904). Part of this overlaps ZM3D's broader decline, but the loss of the reason-to-return loop mirrors July.
  • Open player-facing lives tickets from this window: ZOM-667 and ENG-2400 (both still open, now linked to ZOM-2438).

Why it recurred

This is the same architectural single point of failure, not a new regression. The scheduler is still a single in-process Quantum cron behind a Highlander singleton, event resets are still self-registered Quantum jobs, life regen is still coupled to the same loop, and there is still no watchdog/heartbeat on the scheduler's last tick — the Observability & Alerting page (updated after the July outage) alarms on API 5xx, Aurora, Kinesis lag and crash spikes, but nothing on the scheduler. The latest backend commit is feature work; none of the July remediation shipped. Both outages therefore ran for weeks before a human noticed.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System — Design & Incident Postmortem.

*TL;DR:* the Zombie Match 3D live-ops event/lives scheduler has now fallen over the *same way twice*. *What happened*
• *Jul 12–26 2025 (summer):* scheduler stalled ~2 weeks → no events fired + lives stopped regenerating. Warehouse marks Plague Race (Jul 7) & Zombie Lane (Jul 14) `failed – "backend scheduler stopped"`. Store revenue ~30% down across the window. No ticket was cut at the time.

*Real impact of the recurrence (warehouse = source of truth)*
• Nov 10 Endless Monster Mode: 526 participants vs ~2,000 healthy, 7% completion vs ~47%, $11 event revenue vs ~$316.

*Broken by design, not a regression.* Scheduler is a single in-process Quantum cron behind one Highlander singleton (`match3d-backend`); event resets are self-registered Quantum jobs; lives regen rides the same loop; and there's still *no watchdog/heartbeat on the scheduler's last tick* (Observability alarms on API/Aurora/Kinesis/crashes — nothing on the scheduler). So both outages ran for weeks before anyone noticed. Latest backend commit is feature work — *none* of the July remediation (watchdog, decouple lives, failover, reconciler, last-tick dashboard) ever shipped.

• Filed *ZOM-2438* — "Live-Ops scheduler resilience — build the July 2025 outage remediation (recurred Nov 2025)", assigned Douglas, with the never-built remediation items + acceptance criteria: https://linear.app/harmonygames-games/issue/ZOM-2438
• Connected the open lives tickets to it: *ZOM-667* and *ENG-2400* (both still open) — linked + cross-referenced.

Done. Here's the story, straight, and what I put in place.

## What's really going on

Your déjà vu is correct — this is **one problem that has now failed the exact same way twice**, not two separate incidents.

**The summer outage (Jul 12–26, 2025):** The Zombie Match 3D live-ops scheduler stalled for ~2 weeks. Events stopped firing and lives stopped regenerating together (they're coupled), and store revenue dropped ~30%. No ticket was ever cut; it was reconstructed after the fact into the Confluence *Live-Ops Event Engine* postmortem — which listed 5 remediation items.

**The recurrence (~Nov 10 – early Dec 2025):** Same failure. The warehouse (`LIVE_OPS.EVENTS.LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE`) records Endless Monster Mode (Nov 10) as *degraded — "tournament scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks."* Support flagged it in #live-incidents, players lost lives/refills with no way to earn them back, and it was only cleared by a **manual restart**.

## Real impact (from the warehouse, the designated source of truth)
- Nov 10 Endless Monster Mode: **526 participants vs ~2,000** healthy, **7% completion vs ~47%**, **$11 event revenue vs ~$316**.
- ZM3D daily revenue **~$151/day → ~$131/day** (Nov 10–Dec 7) = **~13% dip, ~$545 below baseline**; DAU **−12%**. (I flagged honestly that part of this overlaps ZM3D's broader decline.)

## Broken by design, or a regression? — **By design.**
Confirmed in `match3d-backend`: the scheduler is a single **in-process Quantum cron behind one Highlander singleton**, event resets are self-registered Quantum jobs, lives regen rides the same loop, and there is **no watchdog/heartbeat on the scheduler's last tick** (Observability alarms on everything *except* the scheduler). That's why both outages ran for weeks unnoticed. The latest backend commit (Oct 12, 2025) is feature work — **none of the July remediation shipped**, and no ticket for it ever existed. Undeniable.

## What I changed (tracking only — no config/scheduling touched)
1. **Filed ZOM-2438** ("Live-Ops scheduler resilience — build the July 2025 outage remediation (recurred Nov 2025)"), Urgent, assigned Douglas, with the 5 never-built items + a 6th (alert routing) and acceptance criteria.
2. **Connected the floating lives tickets** — linked ZOM-667 and ENG-2400 on ZOM-2438 and cross-referenced them with comments.
3. **Updated the Live-Ops Event Engine postmortem** (v9) with the Nov recurrence, the impact, and the "not built" status on every remediation line.
4. **Posted a status in #live-incidents** tagging Douglas + Arthur as owners of the fix.

One judgment call to flag: ENG-2400 is DD-tagged, but it's an open "lives not generating" ticket in the same cluster and was discussed alongside this in #live-incidents, so I connected it and noted the DD scope explicitly rather than dropping it.
